unit.title: At the Bank
objectives: I can understand a bank conversation about opening an account, digital payments, credit cards, and wire transfers.
I can use banking words such as deposit, balance, interest, and wire transfer.
I can ask simple questions at a bank counter.
unit.source: ALL+ 互動英語 2026年8月號 p.51

passages.title: A Student at the Bank
passages.transcript: Customer: Hi. I'm a student from Taiwan, and I want to open an account here. Clerk: Sure. A checking account is for everyday spending, and a savings account lets you save money and earn interest. Customer: Then I'll take both, please. Clerk: No problem. Please show me your passport, your student visa, your I-20 form, and something that proves your address. You don't need a Social Security Number. Customer: Here you go. Can I use my new account with Zelle or PayPal? Clerk: Yes. Zelle is already inside our mobile app, so you only need a phone number or an email address. For PayPal, create a PayPal account first and then link it to your bank account. And please turn on two-factor authentication for extra security. Customer: Got it. Clerk: One more thing. Would you like a student credit card? It helps you build a credit history. Customer: Sounds useful. I'll apply. Clerk: Welcome back! Customer: My parents sent me money by wire transfer three days ago, but it hasn't arrived yet. Clerk: A wire transfer normally needs three to five business days to arrive. A wrong SWIFT code or extra security checks can also cause a delay. Do you have the reference number? Customer: Yes, here it is. Clerk: Thank you. Let me check the status for you.

sets.title: Listening 1 · A Student at the Bank

questions.stem: Which account helps you save money and earn interest?

options.feedback: The clerk says a checking account is for everyday spending. Listen again for "earn interest".
The credit card comes later and is for building a credit history. Listen to the first part again.

questions.explanation: The clerk says a savings account lets you save money and earn interest. A checking account is for everyday spending. savings account 儲蓄帳戶；checking account 支票／活期帳戶.

hints.text: Listen again to the first part. The clerk compares two accounts.
Listen slowly. Key words: everyday spending / earn interest.
"A checking account is for everyday spending, and a ___ account lets you save money and earn interest."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: a savings account.

questions.stem: Which item does the customer NOT need to open the account?

options.feedback: The clerk asks for the passport first. Listen for the word "don't".
The student visa is on the clerk's list. Which item does the clerk say is not needed?
The clerk asks for "something that proves your address". Listen for "You don't need ...".

questions.explanation: The clerk lists a passport, a student visa, an I-20 form, and something that proves the customer's address, then says, "You don't need a Social Security Number." 國際學生開戶不一定需要 SSN（美國社會安全號碼）.

hints.text: Listen again. The clerk gives a list, then says one thing is not needed.
Listen slowly. Key words: "You don't need ...".
"Please show me your passport, your student visa, your I-20 form, and something that proves your address. You don't need a ___."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: a Social Security Number.

questions.stem: How long does a wire transfer usually take?

options.feedback: Listen again: the clerk gives a range of days, not just one.
Two weeks is not mentioned. Listen for "normally needs".
Three days is when the parents SENT the money, not how long a transfer usually takes.

questions.explanation: The clerk says a wire transfer normally needs three to five business days to arrive. business days = 工作天（不含週末、假日）.

hints.text: Listen to the last part of the conversation. Focus on numbers.
Listen slowly. Key words: normally needs.
"A wire transfer normally needs ___ to ___ business days to arrive."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: three to five business days.

questions.stem: According to the clerk, what can cause a wire transfer to be late?

options.feedback: Zelle and PayPal are from an earlier part of the talk. Listen for the word "delay".
The credit card is not connected to the transfer. Listen for what "can also cause a delay".
No day of the week is mentioned. Listen for "wrong".

questions.explanation: The clerk says a wrong SWIFT code or extra security checks can cause a delay. SWIFT code = 銀行國際代碼，用於國際匯款辨識收款銀行.

hints.text: Listen to the wire transfer part again.
Listen slowly. Key words: cause a delay.
"A wrong ___ code or extra security checks can also cause a delay."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: a wrong SWIFT code.

questions.stem: I want to put NT$5,000 into my savings account. I'd like to make a ___.

options.feedback: A withdrawal means taking money OUT. The speaker is putting money IN.
A loan is money you borrow from the bank. The speaker is giving money to the bank.

questions.explanation: make a deposit = put money into an account（存款）; make a withdrawal = take money out（提款）.

hints.text: Is the speaker putting money IN or taking money OUT?
make a ___ = 存款.
Option B is the opposite (taking money out).
Answer: deposit. Try the similar question below.

questions.stem: Before I buy the concert ticket, let me check my account ___ to see how much money I have left.

options.feedback: A visa lets you enter a country. We need a word for the amount of money in an account.
A mortgage is a loan for buying a house. Read "how much money I have left".

questions.explanation: balance = the amount of money in your account（餘額）.

hints.text: The speaker wants to know "how much money I have left".
words: how much money I have left

hints.text: You need a noun meaning 餘額.
Option A (visa) is for travel, not money.
Answer: balance. check your balance = 查餘額.

questions.stem: With two-factor ___, you need your password AND a code sent to your phone to log in.

options.feedback: Compliance means following rules or laws. The sentence is about proving who you are.
A purchase is something you buy. Logging in is not buying.

questions.explanation: two-factor authentication = 雙重認證: you prove who you are in two ways (password + phone code). It adds security.

hints.text: You need TWO things to log in. What does this check?
You need a word meaning 驗證、認證.
Option C (purchase) is about buying.
Answer: authentication.

questions.stem: My parents in Taiwan sent money to my bank account in Canada by wire t________.
questions.explanation: wire transfer = 電匯: sending money from one bank to another, often between countries.

hints.text: Money moves from one country's bank to another.
The word starts with t and means 轉帳、匯款.
It has 8 letters: t r a n s _ _ _.
Answer: transfer → wire transfer.

questions.stem: You want to know whether a credit card costs money every year. What should you ask the bank clerk?

options.text: Do I have to pay a yearly fee for this card?
Can I make a withdrawal from my savings account?
options.feedback: This asks about taking money out, not about the card's cost.

options.text: How do I link my account to PayPal?
options.feedback: This is about digital payments. You want to know about a cost every year.

questions.explanation: a yearly (annual) fee = 年費. Other useful questions: How is interest calculated? Can the fee be waived (免除)?

hints.text: Key words in the question: "costs money every year".
Money you pay every year = a yearly / annual fee（年費）.
Option C is about PayPal, not the card.
Answer: A.

variants.stem: I need cash for the night market, so I'll make a ___ from the ATM.
variants.explanation: Taking cash out of an account = make a withdrawal（提款）.
